ch1_fundamentals.topic: Absence of Partnership Deed — Statutory Rules
ch1_fundamentals.question: A, B and C are partners without a deed. A claims 10% interest on capital; B claims ₹2,000 monthly salary; C claims 10% on loan of ₹50,000. How are disputes resolved?
solution_steps: Apply Section 13 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932:
• Interest on Capital: Not allowed to A.
• Partner Salary: Not allowed to B.
• Interest on Partner Loan: Allowed strictly @ 6% p.a. to C (₹3,000).
• Profit Sharing: Equally among A, B, and C (1:1:1).
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Statutory rule: In the absence of an agreement, Section 13 mandates equal profit sharing and restricts interest on loan to 6% p.a.

ch1_fundamentals.topic: P&L Appropriation Account with Interest on Drawings
ch1_fundamentals.question: Anubha & Kajal share in 2:1. Capitals: ₹90,000 and ₹60,000. Interest on Capital @ 5% p.a. Interest on Drawings @ 5% p.a. (Drawings: ₹8,500 and ₹6,500). Net Profit ₹45,000.
solution_steps: 1. Interest on Capital: Anubha = ₹4,500, Kajal = ₹3,000 (Total ₹7,500).
2. Interest on Drawings (average 6 months): Anubha = ₹213, Kajal = ₹163 (Total ₹376).
3. Divisible Profit = ₹45,000 + ₹376 − ₹7,500 = ₹37,876. Distributed in 2:1.

debit.particulars: To Interest on Capital: Anubha (₹4,500), Kajal (₹3,000)
To Profit Transferred to Capital: Anubha (₹25,251), Kajal (₹12,625)

credit.particulars: By Interest on Drawings: Anubha (₹213), Kajal (₹163)

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Interest on Monthly Drawings (Product & Average Period Method)
ch1_fundamentals.question: Calculate Interest on Drawings @ 10% p.a. on ₹2,000 drawn monthly: (a) Beginning of every month, (b) Middle of every month, (c) End of every month.
solution_steps: Annual Drawings = ₹2,000 × 12 = ₹24,000.
Formula: Total Drawings × Rate/100 × Average Period/12.

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Past Adjustments (Omission of Interest on Capital)
ch1_fundamentals.question: A, B and C share in 3:2:1. After closing books, it was discovered that Interest on Capital @ 10% p.a. was omitted. Capitals were: A ₹1,00,000, B ₹80,000, C ₹60,000. Pass an Adjustment Journal Entry.
solution_steps: 1. Calculate total omitted interest: A ₹10,000, B ₹8,000, C ₹6,000 = Total ₹24,000.
2. Profit wrongly credited in 3:2:1 (A ₹12,000, B ₹8,000, C ₹4,000).
3. Net adjustment: A Dr ₹2,000, B Nil, C Cr ₹2,000.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Adjustment Table: A is excess Dr by ₹2,000; C is short Cr by ₹2,000.

journal_entries.particulars:
A's Current/Capital A/c .................................................... Dr.
    To C's Current/Capital A/c
(Being adjustment for omitted interest on capital)

ch2_goodwill.topic: Super Profit Method of Goodwill Valuation
ch2_goodwill.question: A firm earned net profits: Yr 1 ₹36,000; Yr 2 ₹40,000; Yr 3 ₹44,000. Capital investment is ₹2,00,000. Normal rate of return is 15%. Calculate Goodwill on 2 years purchase of Super Profit.
solution_steps: 2. Normal Profit = Capital Employed × NRR = ₹2,00,000 × 15% = ₹30,000.
3. Super Profit = Average Profit − Normal Profit = ₹40,000 − ₹30,000 = ₹10,000.
4. Goodwill = Super Profit × 2 = ₹10,000 × 2 = ₹20,000.
ch2_goodwill.working_notes: Goodwill under Super Profit = (Actual/Average Profit − Normal Profit) × Number of years purchase = ₹20,000.

ch3_admission.topic: Sacrificing Ratio and Premium for Goodwill
ch3_admission.question: X and Y are partners in 3:2. Z is admitted for 1/4th share, acquired equally from X and Y (1/8 each). Z brings ₹50,000 capital and ₹20,000 goodwill in cash. Give Journal Entries and calculate New Ratio.
solution_steps: 1. Sacrificing ratio of X and Y = 1/8 : 1/8 = 1:1.
3. Premium for goodwill (₹20,000) is distributed equally (₹10,000 each).
ch3_admission.working_notes: Sacrificing Ratio = Old Share − New Share = 1:1. Z's capital and goodwill recorded via Bank A/c.

journal_entries.particulars:
Bank A/c .......................................................................... Dr.
    To Z's Capital A/c
    To Premium for Goodwill A/c
(Being capital & goodwill brought in cash)

Premium for Goodwill A/c ............................................. Dr.
    To X's Capital A/c
    To Y's Capital A/c
(Being goodwill credited to sacrificing partners in 1:1)

ch3_admission.question: A & B (3:2) admit C for 1/5th share. Assets revalued: Land appreciates by ₹20,000, Machinery depreciates by ₹5,000, Provision for Doubtful Debts created @ 5% on Debtors of ₹40,000 (₹2,000). Prepare Revaluation A/c.
solution_steps: 1. Credit Revaluation with increase in Assets: Land ₹20,000.
2. Debit Revaluation with decrease in Assets / increase in Liabilities: Machinery ₹5,000, PBDD ₹2,000.
3. Profit on Revaluation = ₹20,000 − ₹7,000 = ₹13,000 transferred in 3:2.

debit.particulars: To Provision for Doubtful Debts A/c
To Profit Transferred to Capital: A (₹7,800), B (₹5,200)

ch4_retirement.topic: Retirement: Gaining Ratio & Treatment of Goodwill
ch4_retirement.question: A, B and C are partners sharing in 4:3:2. B retires. B's share is taken over by A and C in the ratio 2:1. Firm's goodwill is valued at ₹72,000. Record Journal Entry for Goodwill.
solution_steps: 1. B's share of Goodwill = ₹72,000 × 3/9 = ₹24,000.
2. Gaining Ratio of A and C = 2:1.
3. Debit Continuing Partners (A and C) in Gaining Ratio and Credit Retiring Partner (B).
ch4_retirement.working_notes:
A's contribution = ₹24,000 × 2/3 = ₹16,000; C's contribution = ₹24,000 × 1/3 = ₹8,000.
Rule: Gaining Partners' Capital A/c Dr. to Retiring Partner's Capital A/c.

journal_entries.particulars:
A's Capital A/c ................................................................ Dr.
C's Capital A/c ................................................................ Dr.
    To B's Capital A/c
(Being B's share of goodwill adjusted through continuing partners in gaining ratio 2:1)

ch5_dissolution.question: Pass Journal Entries on dissolution: (a) Realisation expenses ₹3,000 paid by firm, (b) Unrecorded asset of ₹12,000 sold for ₹10,000, (c) Creditors of ₹25,000 accepted stock valued ₹20,000 in full settlement.
solution_steps: Apply rules of dissolution under Section 48 of Partnership Act:
• Realisation expenses: Realisation Dr. to Bank.
• Sale of unrecorded asset: Bank Dr. to Realisation for realized amount ₹10,000.
• Asset taken by creditor in settlement: No entry required in accounts.
ch5_dissolution.working_notes: When a creditor accepts an asset in full or partial satisfaction of their claim, no entry is passed for the settlement of that asset and liability value.

journal_entries.particulars:
Realisation A/c .............................................................. Dr.
    To Bank A/c
(Being realisation expenses paid by firm)

Bank A/c .......................................................................... Dr.
    To Realisation A/c
(Being unrecorded asset realized in cash)
No Journal Entry Required (Creditor accepted asset in settlement)

ch7_shares.topic: Pro-Rata Allotment and Call in Arrears Calculation
ch7_shares.question: Sun Pharma Ltd. issued 50,000 shares of ₹10 at ₹2 premium (₹3 App, ₹5 Allotment incl. premium, ₹4 Call). Received 70,000 applications. 10,000 rejected, pro-rata to 60,000. Ramesh (1,000 shares allotted) failed to pay allotment and call. Forfeit his shares.
solution_steps: 4. Forfeiture entry: Debit Share Capital ₹10,000, Debit Securities Premium ₹2,000.
ch7_shares.working_notes: Share Capital Dr. (1,000 × ₹10) = ₹10,000; Securities Premium Dr. (unpaid) = ₹2,000; Calls in Arrears = ₹4,400 + ₹4,000 = ₹8,400; Share Forfeiture (paid towards capital) = ₹3,600.

journal_entries.particulars:
Equity Share Application A/c ........................................... Dr.
    To Equity Share Capital A/c (50,000 × ₹3)
    To Equity Share Allotment A/c (Advance)
    To Bank A/c (10,000 rejected × ₹3)

Equity Share Capital A/c (1,000 × ₹10) ............................ Dr.
Securities Premium A/c (1,000 × ₹2) ............................. Dr.
    To Calls in Arrears A/c (₹4,400 + ₹4,000)
    To Share Forfeiture A/c (1,000 × ₹3 + ₹600)

ch10_cashflow.topic: Cash Flow from Operating Activities (Indirect Method)
ch10_cashflow.question: Calculate Cash Flow from Operating Activities: Net Profit before Tax ₹1,20,000; Depreciation on Machinery ₹25,000; Goodwill amortized ₹10,000; Increase in Debtors ₹15,000; Decrease in Stock ₹8,000; Decrease in Creditors ₹6,000.
solution_steps: 1. Net Profit before Tax = ₹1,20,000.
2. Add Non-Cash / Non-Operating Expenses: Depreciation (+₹25,000), Goodwill (+₹10,000). Operating Profit before Working Capital changes = ₹1,55,000.
3. Adjust Working Capital: Decrease in Stock (+₹8,000), Increase in Debtors (−₹15,000), Decrease in Creditors (−₹6,000).
4. Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities = ₹1,55,000 + ₹8,000 − ₹21,000 = ₹1,42,000.
ch10_cashflow.working_notes: Formula: Operating Profit before Working Capital changes + Decrease in Current Assets + Increase in Current Liabilities − Increase in Current Assets − Decrease in Current Liabilities.

ch2_fundamentals.topic: Statutory Rules in Absence of Partnership Deed
ch2_fundamentals.question: State the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 regarding: (a) Salaries, (b) Interest on capital, (c) Interest on loan, (d) Sharing of profits.
solution_steps: • (a) No salary or commission is payable to any partner.
• (b) No interest is allowed on capital.
• (c) Interest on loan is paid @ 6% p.a.
• (d) Profits and losses are shared equally (1:1).
ch2_fundamentals.working_notes: Governed under Section 13 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.

ch2_fundamentals.topic: Guarantee of Minimum Profit to a Partner
ch2_fundamentals.question: A, B and C share in 5:4:1. C is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹30,000 p.a. Any deficiency is to be met by A and B equally. Firm earns profit of ₹2,00,000. Prepare P&L Appropriation A/c.
solution_steps: 2. C's deficiency = ₹30,000 guaranteed − ₹20,000 actual = ₹10,000.
3. Deficiency met equally by A and B (₹5,000 each). Final: A ₹95,000, B ₹75,000, C ₹30,000.
ch2_fundamentals.working_notes: Deficiency sharing: A deducts ₹5,000; B deducts ₹5,000; C receives ₹10,000 addition.

debit.particulars: To Profit Transferred to Capital: A (₹95,000), B (₹75,000), C (₹30,000)

ch9_ratios.question: Current Liabilities of a firm are ₹1,50,000. Its Current Ratio is 3:1 and Liquid Ratio is 1.2:1. Calculate value of Inventory (Stock).
solution_steps: 1. Current Assets = Current Ratio × Current Liabilities = 3 × ₹1,50,000 = ₹4,50,000.
2. Liquid Assets = Liquid Ratio × Current Liabilities = 1.2 × ₹1,50,000 = ₹1,80,000.
3. Inventory = Current Assets − Liquid Assets = ₹4,50,000 − ₹1,80,000 = ₹2,70,000.
ch9_ratios.working_notes: Formula: Quick Assets = Current Assets − (Inventory + Prepaid Expenses). Assuming Prepaid Expenses = Nil, Inventory = ₹2,70,000.

ch_journal.topic: Trade Discount vs Cash Discount Journal Entries
ch_journal.question: Sold goods to Mohan of list price ₹20,000 at 10% trade discount and 2% cash discount. Mohan paid 50% immediately by cheque. Pass journal entry.
solution_steps: 1. List Price = ₹20,000. Less: 10% Trade Discount (₹2,000). Net Sale Price = ₹18,000.
2. Cash component (50%) = ₹9,000. Cash discount @ 2% on ₹9,000 = ₹180. Cheque received = ₹8,820.
3. Credit component (50%) = ₹9,000 recorded in Mohan's account.
ch_journal.working_notes: Trade discount is never recorded in the books of accounts; cash discount is allowed only on the amount paid immediately.
